title: House-rules Roadmap
eyebrow: Design · 226 open issues triaged into eight phases, worked one at a time

short.lead: All 226 open issues were read and checked against the code. 145 are still needed and 37 need a closer look, while 38 are already built, duplicated or replaced, and 6 are built on the branch AjsAgent/session-handoff but not merged. The proposal: close every one of the 226, and open one issue per phase in their place. Each phase issue lists every old issue it absorbs, so nothing is lost. The phases run one at a time, each with its own design, plan and QA (your testing pass), and the next starts only when the one before it passes. Phase 2 makes any of your four accounts pick up where another stopped, tested on your accounts, the desktop app and the cloud. Phase 4 makes every page fit its idea, show its work and follow the calm-by-default research on pages for ADHD and autistic readers. The full per-issue verdicts are in docs/2-roadmap/triage/.
short.hint: Tap a phase to see what it covers, the old issues it absorbs, and what done looks like.

items.alt: Eight numbered boxes in two rows of four, joined by arrows. The top row, 1 to 4: approvals just work, pick up on any of your four accounts, the guard refuses only what can't be undone, and pages that fit, show the work and stay calm. The bottom row, 5 to 8: helpers you can follow, your credit everywhere, docs and changelog, and the plugin split with faster hooks.
items.caption: The phases run left to right, top row first.

items: plus
Phase 1, 22 issues
Approvals and the design loop just work

Every way you approve moves the stage, and the plugin never offers you a line or a button that won't work. A fault found in QA goes back to Build with one message, and "skip design" covers one change across its files. Absorbs the approval issues (#491, #481, #475, #429, #379, #296, #273, #155, #141, #131, #132) and the design-loop flow issues (#480, #459, #460, #458, #457, #110, #107, #128, #129, #130, #102). The five approvals that moved nothing today become its first tests.
Done when each of today's failed approvals gets the right answer, a QA fix needs one message from you, and both pass a real session in the desktop app.
plus
Phase 2, 17 issues
Pick up on any of your four accounts

Finishes the session handoff already on the branch AjsAgent/session-handoff: a save per folder (no folder erases another's work), the pickup and its restore, and a save when a usage limit cuts a turn off. It also adds one command that points the desktop app and cloud sessions at a branch build and back, so every later phase can be tested where you use it. Takes in #406 to #410, #486 to #489, #140, #479, #44, #46, #137, #202, #205 and #215.
Finished when work started on one account is picked up on another, in the desktop app and in a cloud session, by steps you follow yourself on a second account.
plus
Phase 3, 17 issues
The command guard refuses only what can't be undone

Routine, recoverable commands run without a prompt, and every refusal names a way forward that works. Permission prompts are readable and never leave a helper stalled. Carries #476 to #478, #484, #285, #200, #189, #156, #142, #145 to #147, #149, #152, #159, #196 and #260.
Complete when a recorded day of real commands runs with no refusal of a recoverable action, and a helper never waits on a prompt nobody can answer.
plus
Phase 4, 36 issues
Pages that fit the idea, show the work, and stay calm

Every proposal and build plan carries a picture of what it changes. Every build plan also shows the code each step will write, editable on the page, before it is written. When the standard layout doesn't fit an idea, the page gets a layout made for it, and a design page can offer you two or three looks to pick from. The builder checks what a page must carry (the choice, the approval line, the picture, the plain summary), not its shape, so no page is skipped for not fitting. Every page follows the calm-by-default research in the focus-deck-app repo (docs/plans/calm-by-default.md, on its branch AjsAgent/sort-steps). That means showing less at once with detail on request, a predictable layout, literal words, calm colour, motion you control and a clear next step. Related items sit together, and colour and icons that give a quick glance always have their words beside them. Pictures go inside the page and the copy box works wherever it opens. Brings in #490, #462, #313, #302, #158, #464, #466, #377, #378, #411 to #417, #419 to #424, #461, #468 to #473, #283, #284, #194 and #297 to #300. The accessibility plugin's own design (#448) stays in phase 8, built on what this phase proves.

Complete when a build plan shows its planned code and a picture, and an idea that doesn't fit the template still gets a page in a fitting layout. Every page also passes a calm-by-default check, with its pictures and copy box working once published.
plus
Phase 5, 31 issues
Helpers you can follow, and that behave

Every helper's progress and transcript one tap away, stall alerts that fire once per stall, and builder rules that stop repeated runs, over-testing and constant status-checking. Folds in the stall-check issues (#120, #123 to #125, #127, #150), the visibility issues (#396, #400, #403, #430 to #436) and the builder issues (#304, #69, #95, #138, #139, #160, #172, #201, #218 to #222, #455, #474).
Proven when a real build with two helpers can be followed from your phone and no helper reruns a check it already ran.
plus
Phase 6, 16 issues
Your credit everywhere, and your names configurable

No Claude credit reaches any repo you own, checked on GitHub as well as locally; the agent's name, credit and branch prefix come from one setting. Gathers #350 to #355, #174, #177, #179, #180, #181, #182, #191, #287, #321 and #405.
Met when a pull request opened from a cloud session carries your credit and the GitHub check refuses one that doesn't.
plus
Phase 7, 16 issues
Docs and a changelog that keep themselves current
A changelog in every repo, a research-and-sources tier, and a check per house rule. Brings in #384 to #388, #336, #45, #117, #228, #244, #301, #399, #404, #436, #463 and #199.
Settled when a pull request that changes behaviour without a changelog line is flagged, in this repo and one other.
plus
Phase 8, 22 issues
The plugin split, and faster hooks

House-rules split into the nine plugins and a shared library already designed, with hook speed and the duplicated code paths fixed on the way. Replaces #437 to #450, #41 to #43, #62, #204, #206, #382 and #482.
Closed when the nine plugins install together on a fresh machine and every hook runs at least as fast as today.
check
No new work, 38 issues
Already built, duplicated or replaced

21 already built (for example #454 and #465, the rerun limit, at safe_git.py:533-603), 10 duplicates (#389 to #395 repeat #411 to #417), and 7 replaced by later issues. Each closes with a comment naming the evidence or the issue that replaced it.
Nothing beyond your approval.
search
You decide
The order, the other products, and how the closes happen
you

Question 1 asks the order of phases 1, 2 and 4, question 2 what happens to the 17 issues about other products (art-pipeline, Eldritch goose, Focus Deck, the Unity workflow), and question 3 when the old issues close.
Answer questions 1, 2 and 3 below.

choices: q1
1. In what order do phases 1, 2 and 4 run?
A
Approvals first, then picking up on any account
Every later phase needs your approvals to register, so fixing them first saves a round trip on every design and plan after it. Phase 2 starts as soon as phase 1 passes QA.
B
Picking up on any account first
Multi-account continuity arrives sooner, but its own design and plan approvals still run on the current loop, with today's friction.
C
Approvals, then pages, then picking up on any account
Phase 4, pages that fit and show their work, comes second, so every later design and plan is easier to read. Phase 2, pickup on any account, waits one place longer.
The other phases follow in the order shown; any phase can be moved later by a dated decision entry.
q2
2. What happens to the 17 issues about other products?
A
Closed here, and listed in the roadmap under Other products

Each gets a closing note pointing to the roadmap's Other products section, which names the product and the old issue numbers. The art-pipeline work lives on its branch origin/claude/art-pipeline; Focus Deck's issue belongs in the focus-deck-app repo.
B
Kept open here, labelled as another product
Nothing is closed, but they stay in this repo's open list and keep showing up in the end-of-turn checks.
q3
3. When do the old issues close?
A
All 226 now, each pointing at the phase issue that carries it

One approval of this page closes them, each with a comment naming its phase issue, or the evidence or duplicate. The 37 unsure ones become a check at the start of their phase, so nothing in them is lost. Code on the branch AjsAgent/session-handoff stays and is carried by phase 2.
B
Each phase closes its own issues when it starts
Nothing closes until its phase begins, so the open list shrinks slowly and the stale labels keep triggering wrong end-of-turn reminders until then.
No issue is closed without this approval.

wrapup.summary: A roadmap replacing 226 open issues with eight phases worked in sequence, phase 2 being pickup on any of your four accounts.
wrapup.changing: Nothing yet. The triage is committed in docs/2-roadmap/triage/; no issue is closed and no code changes until you approve.
wrapup.blocking: Your pick of one option in each of questions 1 to 3, or what you want changed.
